ranking_basis: Evidence strength, measurable ordinary-workload relevance, effort/dependencies and correctness/recovery exposure. Rank is investigation/decision order, not an asserted speedup.
shared_validation: measurement-plan.json decision_criteria and matched >=6-pair baseline method apply to every experimental candidate. Native measurements/qualification and owner acceptance remain separate. All effort is relative scope, not a delivery estimate.

candidates.name: Component timing and retained-file read comparison
candidates.layer: Application diagnostic; read and write attribution
candidates.evidence: Saved BF rates include CPU/guard/UI/USB; no syscall timings. Same read+verify rate can mask media changes. Exact source overhead is known.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Resolve which layer deserves optimization; no immediate speedup promised. Prevent spending effort on an unsupported TRIM/media diagnosis.
candidates.workloads: Retained sequential/random/small-file reads first; disposable save/install/write timing later.
candidates.effort: Small-to-medium diagnostic engineering/review; no firmware change. Depends on BF qualification and separate native implementation/release.
candidates.costs: <=8MiB extra memory, timer/event CPU cost measured <=2%, bounded USB output; retain stop/UI schedule and full content controls. Read-only opens may incur OS metadata side effects.
candidates.baseline: Frozen BF algorithm used as reference in a fresh fixed read-only A/B diagnostic; no BF relaunch. CPU-only and syscall-only versus verified-read.
candidates.success: Instrumented scope coverage with unexplained application residual<=2% and timing overhead<=2%, exact bytes/hashes and complete rc/latency distributions; hidden syscall subcomponents remain unknown. Subsequent improvements require>=10% throughput or>=5% approved workload latency gain.
candidates.regression: Shared tail/correctness thresholds; no current BF edit or reduced guards.

candidates.name: Optimize pattern/SHA/comparison and rendering in a future diagnostic
candidates.evidence: Write generates+hashes; read regenerates+compares+hashes. BF uses software SHA and periodic UI. Actual CPU shares remain unmeasured.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Potentially faster integrity diagnostics if CPU timers dominate; ordinary games benefit only if their own measured work shares the optimized component.
candidates.workloads: Capacity/readback tool, not automatically game/save/install stack.
candidates.effort: Small-to-medium after O01; independent known vectors, compiler/ABI and full cancellation/error review required.
candidates.costs: Bounded extra buffers or CPU/vector state; possible PPU/SPU transfer/scheduling overhead. No integrity sampling or weakened full hashes; same content and exact pattern domains/high offsets. UI can suppress redundant redraws while keeping accepted service cadence.
candidates.baseline: Unmodified algorithm/UI in a new separately reviewed tool, paired CPU-only and verified-read runs at identical buffers/order.
candidates.success: >=10% end-to-end diagnostic gain, >=5/6 paired direction, independent full vectors/content equality and <=2% instrumentation cost.
candidates.regression: No tail/stop/UI/cleanup regression; no game speedup claim absent a relevant workload result.

candidates.name: Tune ordinary read request size, alignment and locality
candidates.evidence: BF submits1MiB serial operations; user-visible512B sectors,4KiB fragments and16KiB blocks differ from unknown NAND geometry. Native device queue depth and copy cost unmeasured.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce syscall/copy overhead for sequential loads/installs; could worsen small/random latency or memory use.
candidates.workloads: Game streaming/read-only retained data, file installs and metadata mixes tested separately.
candidates.effort: Small application experiment; medium if changed in shared libfs/driver. First measure4KiB/64KiB/1MiB at QD1.
candidates.costs: Larger buffers use scarce memory and delay cooperative cancellation; preserve <=1MiB service boundaries using slicing. No bypass of cache coherence, fsync/flush or error paths.
candidates.baseline: Exact same immutable ranges and QD1, fixed cache-state labels/compiler/UI; counterbalanced buffer sweep.
candidates.success: >=10% throughput or>=5% approved game/load/install elapsed reduction; no>5%p95/>10%p99 regression for small reads/save-like workloads.
candidates.regression: Full content/offset/EOF equality, no memory-budget increase without benefit and no queue-depth claims from app thread count.

candidates.name: Reduce diagnostic guard/USB overhead only with equivalent safety
candidates.evidence: Two syscall840 calls per1MiB write, STOP-file open per1MiB, progress fsync every256MiB plus boundaries. Repeated call count is confirmed; time dependence is unmeasured.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Remove redundant work only if timers show meaningful share; guard call count alone cannot explain the write step without rising call cost.
candidates.workloads: Future integrity diagnostic only; normal games do not run these guards.
candidates.effort: Medium because ownership/reserve/cancellation invariants need new proof and fault cases. Current BF remains immutable.
candidates.costs: Caching free-space values or STOP handles can hide background allocation or token delivery; cannot reduce reserve enforcement/stop responsiveness/publication reliability. Rank measurement before any cadence proposal.
candidates.baseline: Exact current guard frequency in future disposable app; individual free/STOP/USB timers.
candidates.success: >=10% diagnostic end-to-end gain while retaining every existing per-write reserve check and accepted cancellation/receipt guarantees; otherwise reject cadence change.
candidates.regression: No reserve/cancel/integrity/USB failure regression, tails within shared thresholds; no ordinary-storage speed claim.

candidates.name: Allocation search and metadata locality
candidates.evidence: Actual kernel has preferred/quadratic/linear group search and fragment/cluster bitmap paths; exhausted searches can grow with fragmentation. No current BF per-allocation timing/extents or occupancy threshold proof.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce fresh-file/install/write latency if group search or metadata I/O dominates. Read benefits only through measured locality/cache effects.
candidates.workloads: New installs, fresh file creation, fragmented near-full writes; existing sequential reads are separate.
candidates.effort: Large firmware engineering after attribution; requires exact P13 kernel mapping, lock/soft-update/free-counter/rollback and repair compatibility proof.
candidates.costs: Hints/index caches consume memory and can become stale under allocate/free/recovery; preallocation shifts work and consumes reserve, layout changes require migration. Do not reclaim reserved space or perform populated defragmentation.
candidates.baseline: Matched disposable available-space and extent-shape states, timers/operation counts; distinguish host bytes/time from physical/NAND writes.
candidates.success: >=10% create/install throughput or>=5% install/save latency gain across independent fixture states and no shared read/save-tail regression.
candidates.regression: Exact allocation ownership/counts/alias controls, full rereads, flush/error/cleanup and separately authorized ordinary restart/recovery acceptance. No >=2TB or repair parity inference.

candidates.name: Driver/crypto copying, batching and scheduling
candidates.evidence: Mapped synchronous filesystem requests and ATA DMA EXT builders; encryption is below filesystem mapping. No separate native crypto, copy or device-busy timers.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce copy/crypto/queue overhead if proven; read/write benefit cannot be predicted from link marketing.
candidates.workloads: Bulk reads/installs and concurrent storage; QD1 diagnostic does not assess real game concurrency.
candidates.effort: Large firmware work; exact object lifetime, DMA/cache alignment, locks/completion/error retirement and selected backend proof needed before native fixture.
candidates.costs: Buffers/pinned memory, CPU/SPU scheduling, lock contention, cancellation stalls, ordering and compatibility risk. Never enable asynchronous/NCQ merely because SSD advertises it; retain flush/ordering contract.
candidates.baseline: Current exact firmware on disposable fixtures; one factor at a time and actual command selection/static proof before changing queue implementation.
candidates.success: >=10% relevant throughput or>=5% approved game/install/save elapsed gain across at least2 fixture states with shared tails/correctness thresholds.
candidates.regression: No ordering/alias/coherence/retirement/resource leaks; full data/persistence/recovery gates separate from performance.

candidates.name: SSD revision/workspace and ordinary idle comparisons
candidates.evidence: Vendor sources establish generic GC/cache/overprovisioning behavior; installed Lexar controller/NAND/cache and fill temperature unknown. Filesystem-free bytes do not prove erased flash blocks.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Different sustained-write behavior or ordinary idle recovery could matter after software bottlenecks are separated; no current replacement recommendation or cache-size inference.
candidates.workloads: Sustained installs/writes; game reads/save latency measured separately.
candidates.effort: Medium measurement/logistics, separate genuinely disposable fixture; no forced power/cache/HPA/DCO setting changes.
candidates.costs: Drive cost/endurance/time and new migration/compatibility qualification; leaving filesystem reserve may help allocation but is not guaranteed controller OP. Idle can change temperature/history.
candidates.baseline: Exact model/firmware, occupancy/history/extent/environment matched; balanced immediate-vs30min idle and independent drive-state repeats.
candidates.success: >=10% relevant write throughput or>=5% install/save elapsed improvement with shared read/tail/correctness criteria, reproducible exact-drive result.
candidates.regression: No unsupported model-wide recommendation, no sample substitutions, no reuse of real populated drives as disposable fixtures.

candidates.name: Review flush/error propagation before performance-sensitive firmware work
candidates.layer: Durability prerequisites, not a speed optimization
candidates.evidence: Saved exact kernel fsync/flush analysis distinguishes file fsync from ATA barrier and identifies ignored error returns in bounded paths. Application API success alone is not media persistence.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Correctness gate for future save/install optimizations; may increase latency. No faster-by-skipping-flush proposal.
candidates.workloads: Save/install/fsync and shutdown; no causal claim for BF slowdown.
candidates.effort: Large independent firmware correctness project; reuse static evidence only, no implementation released here.
candidates.costs: Potential performance regression for required durability, complicated locks/lifetime/retirement/soft-update integration and recovery qualification.
candidates.baseline: Current exact fsync/close semantics and required durable contract, not merely current API time.
candidates.success: First prove/check intended ordering and error propagation. Any performance comparison must meet shared thresholds against equally correct semantics; unavoidable durability cost documented, not suppressed.
candidates.regression: No successful-return claim under ambiguous publication/retirement or failed barrier; no power-loss experiments without a separate disposable protocol.

candidates.name: TRIM/discard feasibility research
candidates.layer: Filesystem -> encrypted LBA mapping -> permitted ATA DSM path
candidates.evidence: Exact Lexar word169 advertises TRIM and word69 DRAT/RZAT. PS3 end-to-end issuance/runtime support remains separately classified in capability matrix; absence of observed DSM is not universal absence.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Possible sustained-write/GC benefit only if erased-block pressure is proven and safe end-to-end implementation feasible. Not necessary or sufficient just because no issuance is found.
candidates.workloads: Reused/freed-space writes; initial monotonically allocating fill is not an isolated TRIM experiment.
candidates.effort: Very large/high uncertainty. Requires exact dead/free ownership (including soft updates and pending I/O), nested region/address translation, encrypted read semantics, allocation races, durable commit/flush ordering, errors/fsck/recovery lifecycle and device behavior proof.
candidates.costs: Irreversible data loss if ranges/ownership/order wrong. Zero ciphertext after device TRIM does not imply zero decrypted plaintext in CBC path. Advertised read-zero semantics do not prove safe filesystem behavior.
candidates.baseline: No-discard disposable matched states only after all static/correctness gates and separate explicit implementation/hardware authorization; no command experiment now.
candidates.success: Prove safety/compatibility first, then >=10% sustained-write or>=5% approved install/save latency improvement across matched independent states with no shared tails/read/correctness regression.
candidates.regression: No whole-drive/live-data TRIM, raw pass-through probes, repair lifecycle bypass or populated Lexar experiment.

candidates.name: Keep current stack and capacity workflow unchanged
candidates.evidence: Historical write slowdown is real at application level; cause/universal benefit not isolated. Current capacity qualification remains open.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Avoid unmeasured compatibility/durability regressions and preserve usable current behavior while obtaining attribution.
candidates.workloads: All current games/saves/installs and capacity qualification.
candidates.effort: No firmware work; research/measurement proposal only.
candidates.costs: Observed diagnostic runtime may persist; no performance claim.
candidates.baseline: Existing reviewed P13/final-v16 and saved evidence; ordinary runtime gates stay with capacity owner.
candidates.success: Adopt unless another option meets measured gain/correctness/tail criteria. Keep stable_storage_support false until independent qualification.
candidates.regression: No new commands/settings/app releases or historical workflow replay.

rejected_or_unreleased.option: Skip full hashes/pattern verification, reserve checks or safe stop
rejected_or_unreleased.reason: Changes the integrity/capacity qualification rather than optimizing equivalent work.

rejected_or_unreleased.option: Disable flushes/write ordering or enable volatile cache for speed
rejected_or_unreleased.reason: Durability and recovery regression; PC-side cache state cannot establish PS3 state.
Drive advertisement does not establish host path/queue/link feasibility. Static proof and compatibility review precede any separately authorized experiment.

rejected_or_unreleased.option: TRIM/free all currently filesystem-free sectors or whole populated drive
rejected_or_unreleased.reason: Ownership/encrypted mapping/pending metadata/recovery semantics unproved; destructive and unauthorized.

rejected_or_unreleased.option: Reformat, enlarge fragments, reclaim Sony/UFS reserve, defragment or delete filler
rejected_or_unreleased.reason: Changes capacity workflow/data/layout and cannot isolate cause; larger-layout4TB research remains separate.

rejected_or_unreleased.option: Infer cache size/NAND/controller/thermal throttling from32GiB or336GiB step
rejected_or_unreleased.reason: Allocation, time, host writes and occupancy co-vary; generic SSD examples are not exact Lexar revision evidence.

rejected_or_unreleased.option: Assume SATA generation/absence of advanced commands from console age
rejected_or_unreleased.reason: Exact saved firmware/device evidence is required; declared drive interface and actual negotiated PS3 link are separate.
